claims.text: Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the liquid structure of Ta-based BCC high-entropy alloys near melting.
Full ab initio thermodynamic integration is computationally prohibitive for the stated Ta-based alloy system.
A moment-matched Gaussian Process potential trained exclusively on liquid-state configurations can replace full thermodynamic integration with a perturbation scheme.
The proposed replacement will reduce computational cost by a factor of ten.
The proposed method will predict the melting free energy of Ta-based BCC high-entropy alloys within 5% of the ab initio reference.
Including high-temperature liquid snapshots in training avoids extrapolation errors in the disordered phase.
A GP or Moment Tensor Potential trained on liquid-phase ab initio data can estimate free-energy differences using thermodynamic perturbation theory without full phase-space integration.
Short-range order and local coordination environments govern the relevant representation of the liquid phase.
The machine-learning potential's descriptor captures liquid short-range order and local coordination environments that EAM misses.
The captured liquid local environments provide a bridge between the solid and liquid free-energy states.
Training on liquid configurations provides an accurate energy landscape for the disordered phase.
An accurate machine-learning energy landscape permits free-energy perturbation or integration over only a small subset of states.
Using perturbation theory with the machine-learning potential reduces the number of expensive ab initio evaluations required.
The method is valid only when the training set covers the relevant liquid temperatures and compositions.
Training sets biased toward solid-state or low-temperature liquid structures cause extrapolation errors in the high-entropy liquid phase.
A significant deviation of the predicted liquid radial distribution function from the ab initio reference indicates failure to capture the liquid structure.
